Image 1: Thirteen-panel storyboard reference, used for the overall shot structure, shot sizes, and camera-movement rhythm. Read it from left to right and from top to bottom; panel N is Shot N. It is a line-art sketch: do not adopt its sketch style, black outlines, white background, panel borders or drawn faces.
Image 2: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, a rendered set, not live action. Use it only for the room's layout, the furniture's positions and the light's direction; do not reference its visual content. It contains no people.
Image 3: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 4: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 5: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 6: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 7: Blocking reference of the segment's start: the same place with these people in their places, used only for where each person is and which way they face; take faces and outfits from each subject's own image. It is a line-art diagram: do not adopt its outlines or white background.
Image 8: Subject 1 (Natalie, look S1) character appearance reference.
Image 9: Subject 2 (Sebastian, look S2) character appearance reference.
Image 10: Prop 1 (agreement) maps to this image; use only structure, material, and color, and copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 10.
Image 11: Prop 2 (bag) maps to this image; use only structure, material, and color, and copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 11.
[Subject settings]
Subject 1 (Natalie): Refer to Image 8. 25, the heroine; George's daughter from his first marriage, who agrees to marry Sebastian Klein to pay for her mother's dialysis. Outfit: look S1: An elegant, figure-fitted ivory-white satin bridal gown with thin spaghetti straps and a low sweetheart neckline. The sculpted bodice is fitted, and the skirt hugs her hips before flaring softly into a floor-length hem. A narrow pale-blue satin sash, her 'something blue', cinches the waist. A short sheer tulle veil is pinned at the back of her curls. Ivory satin pointed-toe heels. No jewellery. Signature colour: blue.
Subject 2 (Sebastian): Refer to Image 9. 30, the hero; the scorned illegitimate son of the Klein family, jailed for three days for reckless driving and secretly a billionaire running a plan. Outfit: look S2: A black slim-cut tuxedo jacket with satin lapels, a crisp white dress shirt, a black bow tie, black tuxedo trousers, black patent oxfords, a small white rose boutonnière and the steel-and-black wristwatch. Signature colour: black.
Environment (Sebastian's apartment, living room): Refer to Images 2 to 6. Night, warm lamplight indoors, city lights glowing through the window. Warm brass arc floor lamp at the couch's front-door end and the glass globe pendant over the dining table; city lights glow through the sheer curtains. Quiet room tone, faint distant traffic.
Do not swap the characters' appearances, clothing, actions, positions or dialogue.
[Subjects and relationships]
Only two people appear throughout: Natalie and Sebastian.
[Blocking]
Refer to Images 2 to 6 for the room and Image 7 for the people's places. Axis and camera side for the whole scene: the camera stays on the kitchenette side of the room, by the right wall, looking across toward the front door on the left wall. The back wall, with the floor-to-ceiling window and the white bedroom door, runs along one side, and the charcoal couch is seen in profile. Natalie stands in the open bedroom doorway on the back wall in her ivory bridal gown and veil, with her pale-blue bag over her shoulder, facing into the bedroom. Sebastian, in his tuxedo, stands on the window side of the round coffee table, facing the couch. There is one charcoal three-seat couch facing the window, with the arc floor lamp at its front-door end. One round oak coffee table stands in front of the couch, between the couch and the window, with one blank white sheet of paper and one blue pen on it. One round dining table with two chairs stands between the couch and the kitchenette, near the bedroom door, and a white pillow lies on the dining chair nearer the couch.
[Overall style]
Photorealistic live-action short drama with cinematic lighting. Each character keeps the face and the outfit with its main colour from their reference image throughout. Use each character sheet only for that character: the face from the close-up on the right, the body and outfit from the turnaround on the left; do not render the sheet's layout, white background or multiple views. This segment has 11 lines, in this order: Natalie, Sebastian, Natalie, Sebastian, Natalie, Sebastian, Natalie, Sebastian, Natalie, Sebastian, Natalie. Generate speech only from the lines in {} in the shot list, each spoken exactly once by its speaker; everyone else keeps their mouth naturally closed while listening, and a V.O. speaker keeps their mouth closed or is off screen. Follow the shot list below; do not add cuts or camera moves beyond it. Strictly adhere to the 180-degree rule: within a scene, characters keep their screen sides and the camera stays on one side of the axis. Seamless continuity of action, spatial matching and consistent actor blocking; cut on action. For dialogue prefer static shot-reverse-shot and over-the-shoulder shots, balanced with reaction shots and close-up inserts. Faces stable and clear, consistent with the reference images, with no resemblance to any real actor or actress. Normal human eyes. Natural anatomy and hands. Natural, fluid motion that follows the blocking; characters make subtle, natural movements. Characters, props and environment share one world with matched lighting. Each line ends naturally with breathing room and is never cut off. Authentic performances with micro-expressions. No BGM; generate only dialogue, environmental sounds and action sounds. No subtitles.
[Continuity]
Maintain continuity in the identities, number, appearance, clothing, relative heights, spatial positions, and eyelines of all the characters. The actions in the shot list occur strictly in sequence. Hands are anatomically correct.
[Strictly exclude]
added or missing characters, spatial jumps. subtitles or garbled text on the paper. malformed hands. Dialogue from the wrong character, multiple people speaking at once, repeated or missing lines, lip-sync errors and audio-visual desynchronization. The raw reference images (character sheets, setting plates) appearing as a frame of the video, and starting on a still frame of the setting reference. A fast zoom-in at the start, a fast pull-back at the end, unmotivated whip-pans, tilts, zooms and 360-degree orbits. Axis-crossing, jump cuts, frame skips, flicker and clipping. Face swaps, changes in age or clothing, sudden height shifts, added or missing characters, spatial jumps, and disordered action sequences; props popping in or vanishing, and duplicate characters except mirror reflections. Hand clipping, extra fingers, fused fingers, malformed hands. Subtitles, captions, watermarks and garbled writing; writing and logos other than those on a key prop's reference image, which are copied from it; a phone screen or paper that is not a key prop is shown from the back or out of focus. Black-and-white, monochrome, grayscale, desaturated visuals; hand-drawn, sketch, line art, illustration, comics, animation; storyboard frames, rough sketches, panel borders, gutters and grid layouts.
[Shot list] (13 shots, approximately 28 seconds)
When a previous-shot reference image is given, it is the moment this segment starts from: keep its people's positions, outfits, props and light, and continue from there. Shot 1 keeps its own camera, matching the image's framing only when it frames the same view; do not repeat that frame later.
Shot 1 (0-2s): [Wide shot, locked-off camera, eye-level, from the kitchenette side; bedroom door at frame right, couch in profile at frame center] Natalie stops in the bedroom doorway in her wedding gown and looks into the single bedroom. Sebastian stands on the window side of the coffee table, watching her. <Soft footsteps stop on the oak floor>
Shot 2 (2-3s): [Medium close-up, clean single on Natalie, eye-level, framed tight on her face and shoulders] Natalie turns her head from the bedroom toward Sebastian, her brows raised. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, wary): {One bedroom?}
Shot 3 (3-5s): [Medium shot, over-the-shoulder shot past Natalie's shoulder at the bedroom doorway, eye-level] Sebastian stands by the coffee table and tips his head toward the couch with a relaxed look. Dialogue (Sebastian, in English, easy and unhurried): {Yours. I'll take the couch.}
Shot 4 (5-7s): [Medium shot, locked-off, eye-level, on Natalie in the doorway] Natalie folds her arms across her bodice and lifts her chin. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, firm): {A wedding isn't permission.}
Shot 5 (7-9s): [Medium shot, slight low angle, slow push in on Sebastian at the coffee table] Sebastian picks up the blank sheet of paper and the blue pen from the coffee table and holds them out toward Natalie. Dialogue (Sebastian, in English, amused): {Then set the rules.}
Shot 6 (9-11s): [Wide shot, pan following Natalie from the bedroom doorway to the couch, eye-level] Natalie walks from the doorway to the couch, sets her bag on the floor at the kitchenette end, sits there, takes the paper and pen from Sebastian and leans over the coffee table. Sebastian stays on the window side of the table. <Satin gown rustles>
Shot 7 (11-13s): [Close-up insert, high angle, on the sheet on the coffee table] Natalie's hand writes neat blue cursive on the sheet of paper. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, businesslike): {Married outside. Separate lives in here.} <Pen scratches on paper>
Shot 8 (13-15s): [Medium shot, over-the-shoulder shot past Natalie seated on the couch, low angle up at Sebastian] Sebastian slides his hands into his pockets and looks down at the paper. Dialogue (Sebastian, in English, calm, testing): {No other dates while we're married.}
Shot 9 (15-18s): [Medium close-up, eye-level, on Natalie bent over the coffee table] Natalie keeps writing, then glances up at Sebastian with a firm look. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, crisp, counting off): {My room. My phone. My business. Knock first.}
Shot 10 (18-20s): [Medium shot, locked-off, eye-level, on Sebastian by the coffee table] Sebastian gives a small nod and a half smile. Dialogue (Sebastian, in English, lazy, teasing): {Done. Lock it if you want.}
Shot 11 (20-22s): [Close-up, clean single on Natalie's face, eye-level] Natalie's pen stops on the paper, and she looks up at him searchingly. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, quiet): {When does this end?}
Shot 12 (22-25s): [Medium shot, low angle, slow push in on Sebastian] Sebastian leans one hand on the edge of the coffee table, steady and unbothered. Dialogue (Sebastian, in English, matter-of-fact): {My trust fund clears. We divorce. You walk away free.}
Shot 13 (25-28s): [Medium shot, high angle over the coffee table, Sebastian's hand at the frame edge] Natalie writes one more line on the agreement and taps the pen on it. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, firm): {You pay the lawyers. I'm not paying to escape.}
At the end: Natalie sits at the kitchenette end of the couch in her bridal gown, leaning over the round coffee table with the blue pen over the written agreement; her pale-blue bag stands on the floor at the kitchenette end of the couch. Sebastian, in his tuxedo, stands on the window side of the coffee table, facing her. The white pillow lies on the dining chair nearer the couch.

Image 12 is the first frame.
